Density estimates (number of animals per square mile) of various game species are generally unavailable for the area of the proposed project and adjacent areas.
A huntable population of white-tailed deer, frequent sightings of wild turkey, and a record of black bear killed in the area have been reported by the South Carolina Wildlift and Marine Resources Department (Appendix A, Bad Creek Environmental Report, 1974). The North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission reports:
"The area in question supports low to moderate populations of big game including, in descending order of abundance, deer, wild turkey, boar, and bear; moderate to good populations of small game, particularly gray squirrel and grouse; average populations of wildcat, foxes, hawks, and owls and an unsubstantiated report of panther."
Recent South Carolina Mountain Unit Hunt deer kill statistics (Table 2-4) for the Horsepasture Game Management Area, which includes the site of the proposed Bad Creek Project and the adjacent Chauga Game Management Area, indicate a slight increase in the annual harvest of white-tailed deer.
